notes.heading: Special Courts

notes.heading: Overview
points: NALSA stands for National Legal Services Authority
It is an apex body to provide free legal services to weaker sections of society
Established under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
It ensures that justice is not denied due to economic or other disabilities

notes.heading: Constitutional Basis

Article 39A ensures equal justice and free legal aid
NALSA gives practical implementation to this constitutional goal
Strengthens access to justice for all citizens

Comes into effect from 1995

Senior Supreme Court Judge – Executive Chairman
Other members appointed as per rules
Assisted by Member Secretary and administrative staff

notes.heading: Objectives of NALSA
points: Provide free legal aid to eligible persons
Organize Lok Adalats for speedy justice
Promote legal awareness among citizens
Ensure justice for weaker and marginalized sections

notes.heading: Who is Eligible for Free Legal Aid

Women and children
Industrial workers
Victims of trafficking or disaster
Persons with annual income below prescribed limit

notes.heading: Functions of NALSA
points: Provides legal aid and advice
Conducts Lok Adalats for settlement of disputes
Spreads legal literacy and awareness
Monitors and evaluates legal aid programs

notes.heading: Lok Adalat System

Helps in quick and amicable settlement of disputes
Decisions are binding like civil court decrees
Reduces burden on regular courts

State Legal Services Authority (SLSA) at state level
District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at district level
Taluk Legal Services Committees at local level

notes.heading: Importance of NALSA
points: Ensures access to justice for poor and marginalized
Promotes equality before law
Reduces judicial backlog through Lok Adalats
Strengthens constitutional vision of justice

notes.heading: Challenges
points: Lack of awareness among people
Insufficient infrastructure in rural areas
Limited reach of legal aid services
Delays in implementation of schemes

notes.heading: Recent Developments

Awareness campaigns for legal literacy

notes.heading: Overview

notes.heading: Constitutional Basis

Promotes access to justice for weaker sections

notes.heading: Legal Framework

Decisions are deemed to be civil court decrees
No appeal lies against Lok Adalat award

notes.heading: Types of Lok Adalats

National Lok Adalat
State Lok Adalat
District Lok Adalat
Mobile Lok Adalat

notes.heading: Permanent Lok Adalat (PLA)
points: Deals with public utility services like transport, postal, electricity
Has both conciliatory and adjudicatory powers
Can decide disputes if settlement fails (in certain cases)
Continuous and permanent in nature

notes.heading: National Lok Adalat
points: Held across India on a single day
Organized by NALSA
Focuses on large-scale settlement of cases
Reduces pendency in courts

notes.heading: Cases Taken in Lok Adalat
points: Civil disputes (property, family, etc.)
Compoundable criminal cases
Motor accident claims
Bank recovery cases
Utility bill disputes

notes.heading: Cases NOT Taken
points: Non-compoundable criminal offences
Serious criminal cases like murder or rape
Cases requiring detailed evidence and trial
Matters involving public interest litigation (PIL)

notes.heading: Features of Lok Adalat
points: No court fee required
Simple and informal procedure
Mutual consent of parties is essential
Fast disposal of cases
Binding decisions

notes.heading: Powers of Lok Adalat
points: Has powers of a civil court in settlement matters
Can summon and enforce attendance of witnesses
Can record evidence for settlement purposes
Award is final and binding

notes.heading: Advantages of Lok Adalat
points: Speedy justice delivery
Reduces burden on courts
Cost-effective for litigants
Promotes compromise and harmony
Improves access to justice

notes.heading: Limitations
points: Depends on mutual consent of parties
Not suitable for complex legal disputes
Lack of awareness among people
Limited enforcement in some cases

notes.heading: Importance in Indian Judiciary
points: Reduces pendency of cases
Promotes alternative dispute resolution
Strengthens justice delivery system
Ensures constitutional goal of equal justice

notes.heading: Conclusion (UPSC Perspective)

They promote harmony through settlement

notes.heading: Overview
points: Permanent Lok Adalats (PLA) are a special form of Lok Adalats
They are established for continuous resolution of disputes related to public utility services
Introduced under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (Amendment 2002)
They combine conciliation and adjudication functions

notes.heading: Constitutional Basis
points: Derived from Article 39A of the Constitution
Ensures equal justice and free legal aid
Promotes access to justice in essential services
Strengthens Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) system

notes.heading: Legal Framework
points: Established under Section 22B to 22E of Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
Amendment in 2002 introduced Permanent Lok Adalats
Have statutory backing (not constitutional body)
Operate under supervision of NALSA

notes.heading: Nature of Permanent Lok Adalats
points: Permanent in nature (unlike one-time Lok Adalats)
Located at district or regional level
Deals only with pre-litigation disputes
Focus on public utility services

notes.heading: Public Utility Services Covered
points: Transport services (road, air, rail)
Postal and telegraph services
Electricity and water supply
Insurance services
Sanitation and public health services

notes.heading: Composition of PLA
points: Chairman: District Judge or retired High Court Judge
Two other members with experience in public utility services
Members appointed by Legal Services Authority
Ensure legal and technical expertise

notes.heading: Jurisdiction
points: Handles disputes related to public utility services
Only pre-litigation disputes are accepted
Value of dispute should be within prescribed limit (₹1 crore as per rules, subject to change)
Cannot handle criminal cases

notes.heading: Functions of PLA
points: Attempts settlement through conciliation
Hears disputes if settlement fails (in specific cases)
Ensures speedy dispute resolution
Reduces burden on regular courts

notes.heading: Powers of Permanent Lok Adalat
points: Has civil court powers during proceedings
Can summon witnesses and documents
Can pass binding awards if settlement fails (except in purely non-compoundable matters)
Its decision is final and enforceable

notes.heading: Key Feature: Hybrid Nature
points: First attempts conciliation between parties
If conciliation fails, it can adjudicate (decide the case)
Unlike regular Lok Adalats, it has decision-making power
Unique blend of mediation and adjudication

notes.heading: Advantages of PLA
points: Quick disposal of disputes
Reduces burden on courts
Cost-effective for citizens
Ensures continuous dispute resolution mechanism
Improves efficiency in public utility sectors

notes.heading: Limitations
points: Limited to public utility services only
Cannot handle serious criminal matters
Limited awareness among citizens
Dependence on cooperation of parties

notes.heading: Importance in Indian Judiciary
points: Strengthens Alternative Dispute Resolution system
Reduces litigation burden on regular courts
Ensures uninterrupted access to essential services
Promotes social justice under Article 39A

notes.heading: Conclusion (UPSC Perspective)
points: Permanent Lok Adalats are crucial for efficient justice delivery
They provide specialized dispute resolution for public utility services
They combine conciliation and adjudication effectively
Important tool for reducing pendency and ensuring access to justice
